title: The First Ascent of Mont Blanc
text: Jacques Balmat and Michel-Gabriel Paccard reach the summit of Mont Blanc, an ascent widely regarded as the birth of modern mountaineering as a distinct pursuit.

title: The Alpine Club Founded
text: The world's first mountaineering club is established in London, formalising climbing as an organised activity with shared ethics, records, and community.

title: The Golden Age of Alpinism Closes
text: Edward Whymper's ascent of the Matterhorn marks the symbolic end of the Golden Age, a period in which most major Alpine summits saw their first ascents.

title: First Ascent of Everest
text: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay become the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.

title: Everest Without Supplemental Oxygen
text: Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler prove that the world's highest peak can be climbed without bottled oxygen, reshaping ideas about human limits.

title: All Fourteen Eight-Thousanders
text: Reinhold Messner becomes the first person to summit all fourteen peaks above 8,000 metres, completing a benchmark that still defines high-altitude mountaineering.

title: The Era of Modern Expeditions
text: Improved forecasting, lightweight equipment, and satellite communication transform expedition planning, making remote peaks more accessible while raising new questions about crowding and impact.
